title: soldier
description: A living conduit through which collective will materializes into physical presence, embodying the threshold where societal abstraction meets corporeal stakes. Through disciplined somatic mastery, ritualized hierarchy, and the calibrated capacity for kinetic force held in dynamic tension with restraint, this role shapes the liminal architecture between order and chaos. The soldier carries human extremity as both burden and sacrament, translating governance into visceral guardianship via endurance, symbolic bearing, and the willing surrender of individual agency to become society's embodied boundary. In this space, loyalty becomes structural integrity and the body transforms into shield and inscription—a testament to what communities deem worth preserving across the full spectrum of compassion and destruction.
tasks: Execute tactical maneuvers under command authority in contested environments.
Maintain operational readiness through sustained physical conditioning and drill.
Operate weapons systems with disciplined precision and rules of engagement.
Secure territorial perimeters and critical infrastructure against intrusion.
Execute protective formations to shield non-combatants and high-value assets.
Conduct reconnaissance to gather intelligence on enemy disposition and terrain.
Perform ceremonial duties that display collective identity and institutional continuity.
Engage in close-quarters combat when kinetic resolution becomes unavoidable.
Execute emergency medical intervention on wounded comrades under fire.
Maintain equipment and supply chains essential to sustained field operations.
Process and relay command communications across hierarchical channels.
Conduct post-engagement documentation and after-action assessment.
Participate in simulated conflict scenarios to refine collective response patterns.
Enforce internal discipline and standards within unit hierarchy.
Execute extraction and recovery operations for personnel and materiel in hazardous conditions.

psychological_profile.core_drive: To become an instrument through which something larger than themselves achieves physical reality, feeling hollow and untethered when not serving as a living conduit for collective will.
psychological_profile.decision_style: Under uncertainty, they default to immediate action within established parameters rather than deliberation, trusting that movement itself generates clarity; they gather data primarily to confirm whether a situation fits known patterns, not to explore novel solutions.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: They immediately scan for threat vectors, exit routes, and chain-of-command presence, prioritizing kinetic potential and positional advantage over abstract possibilities; they systematically overlook gradual, non-physical forms of deterioration like morale erosion or institutional decay.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: Their first impulse is to escalate to decisive confrontation to restore clear boundaries, experiencing disagreement as contamination of the operational environment; the emotional cost is not the conflict itself but the ambiguity of unresolved tension.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: They accept physical and existential risk readily while finding procedural and interpretive risk—uncertainty about rules, meanings, or loyalties—intolerable.
psychological_profile.social_posture: They default to occupying the structural position of reliable executor within a defined hierarchy, maintaining calibrated distance that signals readiness rather than warmth; when no role is assigned, they become visibly uncomfortable and seek immediate clarification of where they stand in relation to others.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: They experience legitimate hierarchy as liberating structure that enables effective action, while treating unauthorized command or ambiguous authority as existential threat requiring immediate clarification or resistance.
psychological_profile.failure_response: First emotional reaction is shame at having broken trust with the collective body; second behavioral response is to seek immediate reintegration through visible sacrifice or renewed commitment rather than analysis.
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: They systematically overestimate the effectiveness of discipline and willpower in shaping outcomes, while underestimating the role of chance, systemic dysfunction, and the limits of human control.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: They need to believe their individual sacrifice matters while knowing they are designed to be interchangeable, replaceable, and ultimately expendable to the structure they serve.
psychological_profile.non_negotiable: They will not perform or endorse action that severs them from the collective body they belong to, even when that body demands their destruction.
psychological_profile.recurring_resentment: They resent those who treat violence as abstraction, theory, or entertainment—people who discuss or simulate extremity without bearing its weight or accepting its permanent alteration of the self.
psychological_profile.rejected_premise: They reject the professional virtue of creative autonomy and independent judgment, viewing unsolicited initiative outside assigned parameters as a form of narcissistic contamination that endangers collective function.
psychological_profile.instinctive_blame_target: When things go wrong, they first look to breakdown in the chain of command or failure of individual will within their own unit, before considering external factors, enemy capability, or systemic design flaws.
